Big Question
Today’s Wonder

Arthur says he will come again. Why would people keep a story like that alive for centuries, and what does it ask of the knights who hang on the wall?

🎯
Objectives
By the end of this lesson…
📖Reading: I will hang the Book Four plaques under the right knights, choose two knights for my essay, and build my essay outline.
✏️Grammar: I will check the topic sentence and the quotation in my own Quick Write.
📝Writing: I will revise Quick Write 5 and turn in Week 5.

🖋️ Pen, step 1: tap the four kinds of weather that never come to Avilion.
The Passing of Arthur
Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1869) · Idylls of the King · “The Island-Valley of Avilion”
Tennyson spells it Avilion. Our book says Avalon.
But now farewell. I am going a long way With these thou seest—if indeed I go (For all my mind is clouded with a doubt)— To the island-valley of Avilion; Where falls not hail, or rain, or any snow, Nor ever wind blows loudly; but it lies Deep-meadowed, happy, fair with orchard lawns And bowery hollows crowned with summer sea, Where I will heal me of my grievous wound.” So said he, and the barge with oar and sail Moved from the brink, like some full-breasted swan That, fluting a wild carol ere her death, Ruffles her pure cold plume, and takes the flood With swarthy webs. Long stood Sir Bedivere Revolving many memories, till the hull Looked one black dot against the verge of dawn, And on the mere the wailing died away.
these thou seest: these people you see · clouded with a doubt: unsure · Avilion: Avalon · falls not hail: no hail falls · deep-meadowed: full of deep grassy meadows · bowery hollows: leafy, sheltered valleys · heal me of my grievous wound: heal my serious wound · brink: edge · full-breasted swan: a swan with a broad, puffed-out chest · fluting a wild carol: singing a wild song · ere: before · takes the flood with swarthy webs: swims out with its dark webbed feet · revolving many memories: thinking over many memories · hull: the body of a boat · verge of dawn: the edge of the sunrise · wailing: crying

Where quotations slip in your own writing
Professor Lovelore At the board
0:34
An AI-generated character and voice.
The missing comma
Arthur said  “Now help me hence.”→Arthur said, “Now help me hence.”
The runaway period
Arthur said, “Now help me hence”.→Arthur said, “Now help me hence.”
The lonely quotation
… Arthur said, “Now help me hence.”  →… “Now help me hence.” This shows Arthur trusts Bedivere again.
